name: Digital Marketing
blurb: Funnel economics, omnichannel, SEO/AEO, social, Meta & Google ads, CRM

questions.q: According to Kotler & Armstrong (Unit 1), marketing is the process by which companies:
options: Minimise production costs above all else
Create value for customers and build strong customer relationships in order to capture value from customers in return
Sell whatever is produced using aggressive salesmanship
questions.explanation: The Kotler & Armstrong definition centres on creating value and building relationships to capture value in return.

questions.q: In the evolution of marketing philosophy, which orientation's essence is 'Goods are not bought but sold'?
questions.explanation: Sales orientation (1930s-1950s) relies on aggressive salesmanship — its essence is 'Goods are not bought but sold.'

questions.q: The Customer Orientation philosophy's starting point is:
questions.explanation: Customer orientation (1950s) starts with the consumer — studying needs/wants before producing, emphasising marketing research.

questions.q: In the traditional 4Ps marketing mix, 'Place' refers to:
options: How the brand communicates with the audience
Where and how the customer accesses/buys the product
questions.explanation: Place covers where and how customers buy — storefronts, distribution, and today e-commerce and social commerce.

questions.q: The McKinsey Consumer Decision Journey is best described as:
options: A strictly linear funnel from awareness to purchase
A circular, four-phase loop emphasising continuous evaluation and post-purchase loyalty
questions.explanation: Unlike the linear funnel, the McKinsey CDJ is circular: Initial Consideration, Active Evaluation, Moment of Purchase, and Post-Purchase (loyalty loop).

questions.q: Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC) is calculated as:
options: Average revenue per user × gross margin × lifespan
Total sales & marketing expenses in a period ÷ number of unique customers acquired in that period
questions.explanation: CAC = total sales & marketing expenses in a period divided by the number of unique customers acquired in that period.

questions.q: What LTV-to-CAC ratio is commonly cited as a healthy digital-industry benchmark?
questions.explanation: A minimum 3:1 LTV-to-CAC ratio is the general industry standard; 1:1 means losing money after costs, and very high ratios may signal under-spending.

questions.q: In the B2B 'Buying Center', who are the Gatekeepers?
options: Assistants who control the flow of information
The technical staff who influence specs
The people who will use the product
questions.explanation: Gatekeepers are assistants who control the flow of information; the Buying Center also includes Users, Influencers, Buyers and Deciders.

questions.q: In the Standard Data Flow architecture, which layer anonymizes IP logs, hashes PII and structures event data before forwarding it?
questions.explanation: The Server Layer receives the client event, then processes, validates, anonymizes IPs, hashes PII and forwards structured records to third-party platforms.

questions.q: The AARRR 'Pirate Metrics' framework stands for:
questions.explanation: AARRR = Acquisition, Activation, Retention, Referral, Revenue — used to measure Product-Led Growth.

questions.q: The critical shift from multichannel to omnichannel is fundamentally about:
options: Unifying the customer experience across all channels so the customer perceives a single coherent brand
Focusing only on the highest-performing channel
questions.explanation: Omnichannel is customer-centric — unifying the experience across channels — whereas multichannel optimises each channel in a silo.

questions.q: In the POEM framework, customer reviews, shares and unsolicited influencer mentions are examples of:
questions.explanation: Earned media is organic, free publicity others create about the brand — reviews, shares, mentions, PR, UGC and backlinks.

questions.q: In Lemon & Verhoef's framework, a customer's own mobile device and how they choose to use a product are examples of:
questions.explanation: Customer-owned touchpoints have no brand control and are dictated by the user (their device, how they use the product, their connection).

questions.q: Which of the following is described as a 'vanity metric'?
questions.explanation: Vanity metrics (follower count, raw page views, impressions) look impressive but don't translate to meaningful business results.

questions.q: In the tiered measurement framework, which are 'Primary Metrics'?
options: Click-through rate and time on site
Revenue, CAC/CPA, conversion rate and CLV — tied directly to business objectives
Social sentiment and share of voice
questions.explanation: Primary metrics are directly tied to business objectives: revenue/AOV, acquisition cost, conversion, and retention/CLV.

questions.q: Nike's 2017 strategic pivot, 'Consumer Direct Offense', was fundamentally a move toward:
questions.explanation: Consumer Direct Offense shifted Nike from a wholesale-dependent model to a direct-to-consumer (D2C) business architecture.

questions.q: Kotler's three criteria for an effective market segment are:
questions.explanation: Effective segments show Homogeneity (common needs within), Distinction (unique from others) and Reaction (similar market response).

questions.q: Dividing a market using 'social class, lifestyle, personality and values' is which segmentation base?
questions.explanation: Psychographic segmentation uses social class, lifestyle, personality and values; behavioural uses benefits sought, usage and loyalty.

questions.q: How do the notes distinguish predictive modeling from traditional segmentation?
options: Segmentation predicts the future; prediction looks backward
Segmentation tells you who a customer WAS; predictive modeling tells you what a customer is ABOUT TO DO
questions.explanation: Segmentation is descriptive (who customers were); predictive modeling forecasts individual future behaviour (what they'll do next).

questions.q: Zero-party data is best defined as:
options: Data a customer intentionally and proactively shares (preferences, intentions)
Data bought from a data broker
Anonymous browsing data observed across sites
questions.explanation: Zero-party data is intentionally and proactively shared by the customer; first-party data is observed across owned channels.

questions.q: According to the retention economics in Unit 3, acquiring a new customer costs approximately:
options: 5x more than retaining an existing customer
Half as much as retaining one
questions.explanation: Industry consensus holds it costs about 5x more to acquire a new customer than to retain an existing one.

questions.q: Research cited (Bain/HBR) states a 5% increase in customer retention can increase profits by:
questions.explanation: A 5% increase in retention can produce a 25-95% increase in profits, underscoring the value of loyalty.

questions.q: The key principle behind first-party data collection in a cookieless future is:
options: Track as much as possible without consent
The 'value exchange' — customers share data when they receive tangible utility in return
Collect data first, provide value never
questions.explanation: Customers don't give data for free — they exchange it for value, so brands must design collection around utility first.

questions.q: In the SMART goals framework, the 'T' stands for:
questions.explanation: SMART = Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, Time-bound (a clear deadline).

questions.q: STEEPLE analysis is used to analyse which factors?
options: External macro-environmental factors (Social, Technological, Economic, Environmental, Political, Legal, Ethical)
questions.explanation: STEEPLE examines external macro factors: Social, Technological, Economic, Environmental, Political, Legal and Ethical.

questions.q: Which budget allocation method is described as 'the most logical' because it links spending to outcomes?
questions.explanation: The Objective and Task method determines objectives, identifies tasks, and costs each — tying budget to outcomes, best suited to agile.

questions.q: The SOSTAC planning framework stands for:
options: Strategy, Objectives, Situation, Tactics, Analysis, Control
Situation, Objectives, Strategy, Tactics, Action, Control
Segment, Objective, Social, Tactic, Audit, Convert
Situation, Opportunity, Strategy, Timing, Action, Cost
questions.explanation: PR Smith's SOSTAC = Situation analysis, Objectives, Strategy, Tactics, Action, Control.

questions.q: A core value of the Agile Marketing Manifesto is:
options: Following a static plan over responding to change
Delivering value early and often over waiting for perfection
Opinions and conventions over experiments and data
Silos and hierarchy over cross-functional collaboration
questions.explanation: Agile values include delivering value early and often, learning through experiments over opinions, collaboration over silos, and responding to change.

questions.q: In Spotify's model, a collection of squads working in the same domain is called a:
questions.explanation: A Tribe is a collection of squads in the same domain; a Chapter is a cross-squad speciality group.

questions.q: A typical Agile marketing sprint is structured around a cycle of:
questions.explanation: Agile marketing breaks quarterly campaigns into two-week sprints with planning, execution, review and retrospective.

questions.q: E-E-A-T, the primary quality signal for AI citation, stands for:
questions.explanation: E-E-A-T = Experience, Expertise, Authoritativeness, Trustworthiness — Google's quality signals that drive AI citation.

questions.q: The query 'best organic cat food for kittens' is an example of a:
questions.explanation: Long-tail keywords are specific multi-word phrases with lower volume but clearer intent and higher conversion — more useful for AEO.

questions.q: Which search intent does the query 'Buy Salesforce enterprise license' represent?
questions.explanation: Transactional intent means the user is ready to purchase right now (e.g., 'Buy...').

questions.q: Which technical element is called 'the single most important' for Answer Engine Optimisation (AEO)?
questions.explanation: Schema markup explicitly tells AI engines what type of content a page contains, making it far more likely to be cited.

questions.q: Real-Time Bidding (RTB) in programmatic advertising is:
options: A manual negotiation process using insertion orders
A split-second automated auction for an ad impression that occurs as a page loads
A method of writing ad copy
questions.explanation: RTB is the millisecond auction that powers programmatic ads: a publisher pings an exchange and the highest bidder's ad is served instantly.

questions.q: Under the CPM pricing model, the advertiser pays:
options: Each time a user clicks the ad
Per 1,000 times the ad is displayed, regardless of clicks
Only when a sale is made
questions.explanation: CPM (Cost Per Mille) charges per 1,000 impressions regardless of clicks — best for awareness/reach campaigns.

questions.q: A landing page differs from a homepage because the landing page:
options: Offers general navigation to all site areas
Has a single focused conversion goal with one offer, one message, one CTA
questions.explanation: A landing page is a standalone page with a single focused conversion purpose — essential for matching ad promises.

questions.q: Who first articulated the attention economy with the idea that 'a wealth of information creates a poverty of attention'?
questions.explanation: Herbert Simon (1971) first articulated the attention economy; Michael Goldhaber (1997) later developed it.

questions.q: On TikTok's For You Page algorithm, which signal is described as the strongest?
questions.explanation: Shares are the strongest engagement signal; watch time and completion rate are also very high, while likes and follower count carry less weight.

questions.q: The four stages of a deliberately engineered viral loop are:
questions.explanation: The viral loop = Payload (valuable content), Incentive (reason to share), Frictionless Share, and Conversion (which restarts the cycle).

questions.q: For the viral coefficient (K-Factor), what does K > 1 indicate?
options: The loop is unsustainable and will die out
questions.explanation: K < 1 is unsustainable, K = 1 is steady/self-sustaining, and K > 1 means true exponential virality.

questions.q: Click-Through Rate (CTR) is calculated as:
questions.explanation: CTR = Clicks ÷ Impressions × 100 — it measures how compelling an ad is to those who see it.

questions.q: The IAB/MRC standard defines a 'view' as:
options: Any time an ad is served
At least 50% of pixels visible for a specified period (usually 1-2 consecutive seconds)
100% of the ad visible for 10 seconds
questions.explanation: The IAB/MRC viewability standard requires at least 50% of pixels visible for 1-2 consecutive seconds, reflecting actual human attention.

questions.q: Duolingo's TikTok 'unhinged branding' strategy had which primary goal?
options: Directly sell app subscriptions on TikTok
Earn attention and build brand awareness (installs follow later)
questions.explanation: Duolingo does not try to sell on TikTok — it earns attention and builds awareness, letting conversions happen later via search and word of mouth.

questions.q: The core principle of Conversion Rate Optimisation (CRO) is that:
options: More traffic always beats better conversion
Reducing friction to convert more existing traffic is often more effective than increasing ad spend
questions.explanation: CRO treats design as applied cognitive psychology — reducing friction to convert more of existing traffic rather than buying more traffic.

questions.q: Hick's Law states that:
options: Time to reach a target depends on distance and size
Decision time increases with the number of options/choices
Items that stand out are remembered best
questions.explanation: Hick's Law: decision time increases with the number of choices — so designers limit options at each decision point.

questions.q: The CRO process follows which sequence?
questions.explanation: The CRO process loops: Research, Hypothesis, Experiment (A/B test), Analysis, then Implement a winner or Iterate.

questions.q: The Japanese philosophy of continuous improvement through small incremental steps, applied in strategic design, is:
questions.explanation: Kaizen — continuous improvement through small steps — is step 6 of the strategic design process; a website is never 'finished'.

questions.q: Inbound marketing is best described as:
options: Permission-based and content-driven, attracting customers who choose to engage
questions.explanation: Inbound is permission-based and content-driven, earning attention; outbound is interruptive and promotion-driven. Inbound traffic typically converts higher.

questions.q: In the Meta campaign objective framework, 'Conversions' and 'Catalog Sales' belong to which stage?
questions.explanation: Conversion objectives (bottom of funnel) include Conversions, Catalog Sales and Store Traffic, and require the Meta Pixel/Conversions API.

questions.q: A Meta 'Lookalike Audience' is:
options: A manually defined audience based on interests and demographics
An audience uploaded from a customer email list
A new audience Meta finds by analysing the common characteristics of a source audience
People who already follow the Page
questions.explanation: Lookalike Audiences find new users who resemble a source audience (e.g., high-value customers); Core = manual, Custom = from existing data.

questions.q: The Meta Conversions API (CAPI) is important because it:
options: Replaces the need for any creative
Sends conversion data server-to-server, bypassing browser-based tracking blocked by privacy changes
questions.explanation: The Conversions API sends data directly from the advertiser's server to Meta, bypassing browser restrictions (ITP, ad blockers, ATT) that reduce Pixel data.

questions.q: L'Oréal's AR virtual try-on primarily addresses which barrier to online beauty purchases?
questions.explanation: AR try-on tackles colour/fit uncertainty — the #1 barrier — and products with AR try-on see 2-3x higher conversion rates.

questions.q: In Google Ads, Ad Rank is calculated (fundamentally) as:
options: Maximum CPC Bid × Quality Score (+ expected impact of extensions)
questions.explanation: Ad Rank = Max CPC Bid × Quality Score (plus expected extension impact), so a higher Quality Score can outrank a bigger budget.

questions.q: GA4's default attribution model is:
questions.explanation: GA4 defaults to data-driven attribution (DDA), using machine learning to assign fractional credit across all touchpoints.

questions.q: The key difference of the GA4 data model versus Universal Analytics is that GA4 is:
options: Event-based — every interaction (pageview, scroll, purchase) is an event
questions.explanation: GA4 uses an event-based, user-centric model where every interaction is an event, versus Universal Analytics' session-based hits.

questions.q: Google's Consent Mode v2, when consent is denied, allows GA4 to:
options: Send only cookieless pings and use behavioural modeling to estimate ~85%+ of conversions
questions.explanation: With consent denied, Consent Mode sends minimal cookieless pings and GA4 models conversions, recovering roughly 85%+ of actual conversions.

questions.q: Patagonia's ethical data approach is characterised by:
options: Collecting only what's needed, transparency, first-party focus and clean-room measurement
questions.explanation: Patagonia minimises collection, is transparent, uses value exchange, prioritises first-party data and clean rooms — achieving above-average consent rates.

questions.q: The five stages of the customer lifecycle (Unit 10) are:
questions.explanation: Lifecycle marketing manages Awareness, Consideration, Conversion, Retention and Advocacy, each with distinct content and triggers.

questions.q: A parasocial relationship is:
options: A two-way partnership between two brands
A one-sided psychological bond where an audience member feels a personal connection with a creator or media figure
questions.explanation: A parasocial relationship is a one-sided bond; the trust built with a creator transfers to the products they recommend.

questions.q: Which email type is 'triggered by subscriber actions on-site', such as receipts and shipping updates?
questions.explanation: Transactional emails are triggered by actions — signup confirmations, receipts, shipping updates, password resets.

questions.q: The 4 Ps email copywriting framework is:
questions.explanation: The 4 Ps copywriting technique moves readers from attention to action: Promise, Paint (the outcome), Proof, Push (the CTA).

questions.q: MrBeast's 'parasocial commerce flywheel' works because:
options: He relies solely on YouTube AdSense
Product revenue (Feastables, etc.) funds bigger content, which attracts more viewers and accelerates the flywheel
He avoids A/B testing titles and thumbnails
His products are unrelated to his content
questions.explanation: Free content builds parasocial trust; product revenue funds bigger content, drawing more viewers — a self-reinforcing reinvestment loop.

questions.q: Why does email endure as one of the highest-ROI marketing channels (per the DMA figure cited)?
options: It is free to send unlimited emails
It is action-forcing, cost-effective and measurable, historically returning roughly $38-44 per $1 spent
It requires no permission or list building
It cannot be tracked or tested
questions.explanation: Email is action-forcing, cost-effective, relationship-building, segmentable, measurable and testable — historically ~$38-44 return per $1.
